# Joseph and Aseneth Chapter 11 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 11:3 — tireless vs. unwearying — describing the serving powers

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "tireless powers will serve you" | Literal akopos |
| LOGOS | "unwearying powers will serve you" | More precise rendering of akopos |
| PNEUMA | "unwearying powers will serve you" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS and PNEUMA agree: 'unwearying.' This is the more precise rendering of the Greek akopos (not weary, without fatigue). 'Tireless' (EMET) is acceptable but slightly informal. Adopted LOGOS/PNEUMA.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 11:6 — stings like iron vs. stings sharp as iron

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "stings like iron" | Literal comparison |
| LOGOS | "stings sharp as iron" | Adds 'sharp' for clarity |
| PNEUMA | "stings sharp as iron" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS/PNEUMA add 'sharp' which is implied by the simile. The Greek sidēra (iron) alone implies hardness/sharpness. Adopted LOGOS.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.
